{{Top|ga}} {{Droid |type=Rebel |image=[[File:R3S1-BYOR2-79.png]] |name=R3-S1 |homeworld= |birth= |death= |creator= |manufacturer=[[Industrial Automaton]]{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars By the Numbers|text=Every Droid in Star Wars|video=UQg6aX7lqTA|nolive=1}} establishes that R3-S1 is an [[R3-series astromech droid]], which are manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]] according to ''[[Star Wars: R2-D2 Deluxe Book and Model Set]]''. |line=[[R-series]]''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' |model=[[R3-series astromech droid]]{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars By the Numbers|text=Every Droid in Star Wars|video=UQg6aX7lqTA|nolive=1}} |class=[[Astromech droid]]''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' |cost= |length= |width= |height=1.09 [[meter]]s{{Databank|r3-s1|R3-S1}} |mass= |gender=[[Gender|Feminine programming]] |pronouns=She/her |sensor=[[Color|Black]]''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' |plating=Silver |armament= |equipment=[[Holoprojector]] |affiliation=*[[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] **[[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]] }} '''R3-S1''', nicknamed "'''Threece'''," was an [[R3-series astromech droid]] with [[Gender|feminine programming]] that served as part of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. By [[1 BBY]], she was recognized as [[chief]] of the [[astromech droid]] pool in the [[Great Temple|rebel headquarters]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]], where she was responsible for the upkeep of the base's equipment rather than being assigned to a [[starfighter]]. R3-S1 was vain and argumentative, as well as inordinately proud of her overclocked [[Intellex V]] [[processor]]. When the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] was scrambled to [[Battle of Scarif|fight]] at the [[planet]] [[Scarif]], R3-S1 flew with [[rebel pilot]] [[Barion Raner]] as [[Blue Four]]. Once in the [[Scarif system]], they tried to pass through the planet's [[Shield Gate]] with the rest of [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]], but were not quick enough, forcing Raner to pull up before crashing. They then aided the Alliance Fleet above the planet, some of which ultimately escaped with the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]]. ==Biography== ===Stationed on Yavin=== The [[R3-series astromech droid]] designated R3-S1 and nicknamed "Threece" served the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. She was stationed at the headquarters of the Alliance's [[Massassi Group]] in the [[Great Temple]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]]. Instead of being assigned to a [[starfighter]], she was employed in the upkeep of technology throughout the base, making sure it was up to date and in prime condition. R3-S1 eventually became recognized as the [[chief]] of the [[Astromech droid|astromech]] pool there. [[File:R3-S1_on_Yavin.png|thumb|left|300px|Jyn Erso and Cassian Andor passed R3-S1 on Yavin 4.]] In [[1 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' to [[1 BBY]]. R3-S1 was present in a [[hangar]] of the temple after [[Alliance High Command]] met to discuss attacking the Empire's [[Scarif Deployment|forces]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] in order to obtain [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]]. The meeting ended with a decision not to launch an attack, but the recently recruited rebel [[Jyn Erso]] assembled a [[Rogue One|group of rebels]] willing to follow her to Scarif against the orders of Alliance Command. Erso and [[Captain]] [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]] led the group through the hangar and past R3-S1 before boarding the stolen [[Zeta-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle|''Zeta''-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle]] ''[[SW-0608]]'' and taking off to start the [[Battle of Scarif]]. ===Battle of Scarif=== {{Quote|Pull up!''"
[Grek screams]|quoteend=0|Barion Raner tries to save Vangos Grek|audio=Raner-Grek.flac|}} When the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] was later scrambled from Yavin to aid the rebels on Scarif, R3-S1 was loaded into the [[astromech socket]] of the [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]] flown by [[Barion Raner]], a [[Rebel pilot|pilot]] flying with [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]] as [[Blue Four]]. Upon arriving in the [[Scarif system]], [[Admiral]] [[Raddus]] directed Blue [[Squadron]] to provided cover for the rebel ground forces. In order to reach the surface, all of Blue Squadron raced to pass through the [[Shield Gate]] in the [[planetary shield]] around Scarif, but after [[Blue Leader]] [[Antoc Merrick]] made it through the gate began to close. Realizing that he did not have [[time]] to make it through the closing gate, Raner pulled up in time to prevent him and R3-S1 crashing into the gate and perishing, as [[Vangos Grek]] and another [[pilot]] did. [[File:Raner-R3-S1-RO.png|thumb|right|300px|R3-S1 flew with Barion Raner at Scarif.]] Raner and R3-S1 then joined the other members of Blue Squadron who had not made it through the gate in aiding the Alliance Fleet above Scarif. While chased by three [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s, the pair managed to destroy one of the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Persecutor]]'s'' [[deflector shield generator]] domes, which allowed the [[Star Destroyer]] to later be disabled by [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron's]] [[ion bomb]]s and used to destroy the Shield Gate. With the gate gone, the [[Death Star]] plans were then successfully transmitted from the surface and a portion of the fleet, including some of Blue Squadron, managed to escape from the Scarif [[Star system|system]]. However, Blue and [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadrons]] had lost nineteen pilots and crew during Scarif and an earlier [[Mission to Eadu|mission]] to the planet Eadu and so few pilots were left that the Alliance was unsure if it could even field Blue Squadron when the Death Star [[Battle of Yavin|attacked]] Yavin not long after.{{StoryCite|story=Duty Roster|book=From a Certain Point of View}} ==Characteristics== [[File:R3S1.jpg|thumb|250px|left|R3-S1 was a highly valued part of the Rebel Alliance on Yavin 4.]] R3-S1 had [[Gender|feminine]] [[Programmer|programming]] and a [[Color|black]] [[sensor]]. She was built with silver plating, apart from her [[plastex]] cranial dome, which was transparent with orange markings. The [[R-series]] astromech was equipped with an overclocked [[Intellex V]] [[processor]] and a [[holoprojector]] built into her dome. R3-S1 excelled at organization, which earned her recognition as head of the astromech pool. At some point she picked up a vain programming flutter that resulted in her not working well with others and being competitive to a fault. The [[droid]] was also argumentative and inordinately proud of her overclocked processor. Despite this, she was highly valued by the Alliance. R3-S1 stood 1.09 [[meter]]s tall and, like all R3-series astromechs, was manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]]. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|This is currently R3-BHD. Normally, he'd be R2-BHD with a silver dome, but today we sorted out for the clear dome. So he's an R3.|Brad Oakley|{{StarWarsShow|49AfMlI6bVo|Star Wars Rebels Coming to Celebration Orlando and the Best Star Wars Video Games with Xavier Woods|sw_url=video/the-star-wars-show-episode-40}}}} [[File:Brad_Oakley_and_R3-S1.png|thumb|right|250px|Brad Oakley (left) built R3-S1.]] R3-S1 was created for the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology]] film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. She first received a designation simultaneously in the reference books ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' by [[Pablo Hidalgo]], ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission]]'' by [[Jason Fry]],''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Ultimate Sticker Encyclopedia]]'' by [[Emma Grange]] and [[Shari Last]],''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Ultimate Sticker Encyclopedia]]'' which were all released alongside the film.{{SW|url=news/rogue-one-and-star-wars-40th-publishing-programs-revealed|text=NYCC 2016: ''Rogue One'' and ''Star Wars'' 40th Anniversary Publishing Programs Revealed}} R3-S1 was made by [[R2-D2 Builders Club|R2 Builder]] [[Brad Oakley]] and used the same body and limbs as the astromech [[R2-BHD]], with the [[R2-series astromech droid|R2 unit's]] silver dome being swapped out for R3-S1's transparent one. Because of this, R3-S1 was known as R3-BHD on set. Prior to the shooting of the hangar scene where R3-S1 appears, a dry run for the droid's movements were carried out and a route that would not get in anyone's way was planned. In the non-[[canon]] comic strip "[[Operation: Bunker Bust!]]," which was published in the [[January]]–[[February]] [[2017]] edition of [[LEGO Magazine|LEGO Club Magazine]], R3-S1 can be seen standing in a hangar in the Great Temple on Yavin 4 as a [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber]] prepares for take off during the Battle of Scarif.{{LegoMagazineCite|club=1|issue=January/February 2017|story=Operation: Bunker Bust!}} ==Appearances== *''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' {{1st}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission]]'' {{1stID|R3-S1|''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Ultimate Sticker Encyclopedia]]''}} ===Non-canon appearances=== *{{LegoMagazineCite|club=1|issue=January/February 2017|story=Operation: Bunker Bust!}} *{{LegoMiniMovie|series=Stop-Motion Story|text=Taking out the Trash|video=rFm76OEUgbw}} ==Sources== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of R3-S1}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' {{1stID|Threece}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Ultimate Sticker Encyclopedia]]'' *{{LEGOCite|num=75172|name=Y-Wing Starfighter}} {{C|as Rebel Astromech Droid}} *{{StarWarsShow|49AfMlI6bVo|Star Wars Rebels Coming to Celebration Orlando and the Best Star Wars Video Games with Xavier Woods|sw_url=video/the-star-wars-show-episode-40}} {{ID|R3-BHD}} *''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A -
